witnesses.title: Papyrus Harris 500
witnesses.discoveryLocation: Egypt; precise findspot not stated in the institutional record
witnesses.dateNotes: British Museum classification: 18th Dynasty. No absolute object date is normalized here.
witnesses.condition: Institutional condition summary: fair; bleached with loss and skeletal areas
witnesses.provenance: Purchased from Miss Selima Harris in 1872; previous collection of Anthony Charles Harris
witnesses.rights: Public institutional metadata; object-image reuse terms are separate and not asserted
witnesses.description: The British Museum identifies two Late Egyptian stories on the verso: The Capture of Joppa and The Doomed Prince. This witness association does not assert that the bundled historical edition was translated directly from the museum object.

witnesses.title: D’Orbiney Papyrus
witnesses.dateNotes: ca. 1215 BCE; 19th Dynasty. This is the physical manuscript date, not a separate claim about first composition.
witnesses.condition: Institutional survey records brittle and fragmentary areas; mounted in multiple frames
witnesses.provenance: Purchased from Elizabeth d’Orbiney in 1857; institutional record associates the manuscript with scribe Inena
witnesses.rights: Public institutional metadata; object-image reuse terms are separate and not asserted
witnesses.description: The British Museum identifies this as the only known copy of the Tale of Two Brothers, written in literary New Egyptian and associated with the scribe Inena. The witness link remains distinct from translation dependency.
